thread:
incident-bot: Alert: elevated tail-latency detected for /v1/chat.generate on pool us-east-1 (model rwd-2-medium). p95=3.4s (SLO 1.5s), p99=9.1s. Auto-tag: continuous-batching, tail-latency
oncall-sam: ack. I'm awake and looking. pulling traces and batch heatmap.
runtime-anish: heatmap: https://grafana.re/d/serve/batch-shape?orgId=1&from=now-15m shows spikes of 500-900 token batches forming. Likely coalescing at batch_window_ms=60ms.
infra-lina: are there noisy tenants? can we identify per-key batch contribution quickly?
obs-bot: sample top contributors (last 10m): key=acme-prod (34%), key=experiment-b (21%), key=pipeline-x (9%).
oncall-sam: ok. immediate mitigations we can do: 1) soft ingress cap per-key (tokens/sec), 2) lower batch_window_ms on model pool (60->12), 3) cap max_batch_tokens, 4) switch continuous_batching off if needed. prefer staged.
cs-elaine: CS already alerted Acme and Experiment B; Acme says they sent some very long prompts and are running a backfill.
deploy-bot: Applying ingress soft cap: ingressctl set-rate-limit --scope=per-key --limit=600tps --mode=soft --duration=30m
deploy-bot: applied. change_id=rc-2026-07-11-1
runtime-anish: I see p95 drop slightly to 2.6s within 20s. heatmap shows fewer 700-900 token batches.
oncall-sam: proceed to reduce batch_window_ms to 12ms on rwd-2-medium pool. note: expect throughput drop and GPU efficiency hit.
deploy-bot: redwoodctl runtime update --model rwd-2-medium --set batch_window_ms=12 --set batch_padding=false --reason="tail-latency mitigation"
deploy-bot: rolling update start; parallel=5%; change_id=rc-2026-07-11-2
runtime-anish: rolling applied. p95 now 1.3s, p99 3.6s. GPU utilization down ~35%, throughput down ~40%.
infra-lina: we need a temporary billing note if this stays >24h. ping finance.
cs-elaine: customers reporting improvement. Acme confirms 2x faster responses. Experiment B still has occasional 4-5s responses.
oncall-sam: next step cap max_batch_tokens to 1200 -> 800 for the pool.
deploy-bot: redwoodctl runtime update --model rwd-2-medium --set max_batch_tokens=800 --reason="limit large-token coalescence"
deploy-bot: change_id=rc-2026-07-11-3 applied
runtime-anish: after cap, p99 drops to ~2.1s, p95 ~1.1s. Throughput further -6%.
oncall-sam: hold on continuous_batching toggle for now. Also disabling optional post-rerank step for this model.
deploy-bot: featurectl toggle --target=rwd-2-medium --flag=post_rerank --state=off --reason="latency mitigation"
deploy-bot: toggled. change_id=rc-2026-07-11-4
sre-kai: taking handoff for the day. I'll keep watch for 3h and coordinate with runtime team to run a canary to gradually restore batch_window_ms for low-load pods.
oncall-sam: summary for pager ticket: suspected cause: concurrent long prompts + long batch window -> giant coalesced batches -> queuing and kernel contention -> tail latency. Actions: ingress per-key soft cap 600tps, batch_window_ms 60->12, max_batch_tokens 1200->800, post_rerank off. Observed improvement: p95 3.4s->1.1s, p99 9.1s->2.1s; throughput cost ~45%.
obs-bot: note: created dashboard panel showing per-key batch contribution and histogram of token sizes. saved as: https://grafana.re/d/serve/per-key-batch
sre-kai: follow-ups: - add adaptive batch_window logic (shorten when median token size > X) - per-key adaptive throttles based on token histogram - run experiment with continuous_batching=false on 10% canary - docs: update live mitigation runbook
cs-elaine: CS will send a consolidated update and offer limited credits to top affected customers. Adding notes to CRM.
oncall-sam: leaving thread pinned to pager. If regress, page the day oncall and escalate to eng-ops. Thanks all :thumbsup:
incident-bot: oncall shift change recorded. handoff oncall-sam -> sre-kai at 2026-07-11T14:08:07Z
sre-kai: acknowledged. I'll sync with runtime-anish and infra-lina on the canary tomorrow morning.
